Sam (People Ops): Hi team — quick heads-up: today we're launching our expanded fertility and family-building benefits, effective April 1. Long post but please read 94 key points below and feel free to DM if you have special circumstances. :sparkles:

Priya (Benefits): TL;DR: What94s changing?
- IVF & IUI coverage: up to $20k lifetime reimbursement (previously $5k) for eligible treatments
- Egg/sperm freezing: up to $10k reimbursement
- Fertility medication: added pharmacy reimbursement path (pre-authorization required)
- Care & leave: up to 5 paid appointment days per year for fertility/assisted-reproduction appointments; these are separate from PTO and FMLA-equivalent leaves
- Counseling: 6 sessions with our EAP for fertility-related counseling, plus support group access
- Global note: amounts above apply to US employees; EMEA/APAC will have regionally compliant equivalents — see FAQ for local caps

Liam (Benefits Admin): Implementation notes for admins: benefits portal will show the new plan on April 1. Reimbursements prior to Apr 1 remain under the old limits. To file for reimbursement after Apr 1, submit the standard claim form plus clinical receipts to benefits@redwood.com. We'll fast-track fertility claims (5 business day target).

Nina (Eng): Thanks, huge step! Quick Q: does the 5 paid appointment days stack with parental leave ramp options? Also curious about coverage for clinic travel and overnight stays.

Priya (Benefits): Great Q, Nina. Appointment days are independent of parental leave/ramp programs. For clinic travel/overnight stays, reasonable travel expenses (mileage, lodging when required by clinic location) are reimbursable up to the travel cap; please include receipts and pre-approve with benefits@redwood.com when possible.

Zoe (Legal): Note for managers: any accommodations requested during the treatment period (schedule adjustments, protected absence) should be handled in coordination with People Ops and Legal to ensure consistency with local employment laws and disability accommodations where applicable. Do not promise exceptions unilaterally.

Sam (People Ops): Process checklist for employees: 1) Review the FAQ on the benefits portal (link below). 2) Pre-notify manager if you plan to use appointment days so they can plan coverage. 3) Submit pre-authorization for high-cost procedures if possible. 4) Email benefits@redwood.com for reimbursement claims or questions. Link: https://intranet.redwood/benefits/fertility (FAQ + claim form).

benefits-bot: Reminder: Live Q&A "Fertility Benefits Overview" Thurs 9am PT 94 register at the intranet event page.

Nina (Eng): Appreciate the live Q&A — will there be anonymized case examples of reimbursement timelines?

Liam (Benefits Admin): Yes — we'll present sample timelines and anonymized claim examples in the Q&A. We'll also upload a one-page quick-start guide after the session.

Priya (Benefits): Confidentiality reminder: all medical info is kept private in HR systems. Managers will only get what the employee elects to share for scheduling/accommodation.

Sam (People Ops): One more note: this is part of our broader family-building benefits refresh (includes adoption support and enhanced parental leave guidance). We'll publish a full benefits summary next week and open enrollment guidance for anyone who wants to change benefits elections.

Nina (Eng): Thank you — this will help a lot of folks. :heart:

Sam (People Ops): Thanks everyone. If you have edge cases (immigration/visa impacts, cross-border clinic billing), please DM Priya or email benefits@redwood.com and cc legal@redwood.com.
